comments.text: At risk of falling into the trap 640k is enough ram for everyone or the human eye can't see above 30fps, I'm going to go ahead and say that we are quickly approaching the point where unless you are looking for budget options you will probably be able to get whatever performance you could possibly want even for VR from a laptop with this architecture. Maybe we'll want higher frame rates of 4K or maybe VR is going to get a lot more resolution and frame rates increases, but once I see a laptop with a Zen 3 CPU (I get Intel will probably have a higher performance CPU, but AMD shows more battery life) and an Nvidia RTX 3060/70/80 with a high refresh rate and high resolution screen (maybe 1440p and then you can hook up a 4K monitor via HDMI) I think that it is going to be able to fulfill any gaming tasks I throw at it. 4K is already somewhat difficult to justify over 1440p, So unless you are regularly checking individual pixels I doubt that 8K is going to be that much more appealing, I think higher resolutions will only be needed for VR going forward. I think after this the only thing consumers should be interested in is better battery life and lower costs (I now there's a very good chance applications might pop up and I will be completely wrong, but if that's the case I'd be happy being wrong). Let me know if you have opposing opinions (also I'm talking about average consumers and even hardcore gamers, not professional video editors or scientists running simulations.)
